text.t: 9AM. The all-hands you called. Fourteen faces in a grid, waiting for you to speak. You called this meeting. You no longer remember why.
9AM. The weekly standup. Fourteen faces in a grid. Someone is eating cereal directly into their mic. It is your turn to give an update on the thing you have not started.

go.msg: A classic. Technically, deciding to start is progress. Nobody follows up. Nobody ever follows up.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it.

go.msg: Radical honesty. The manager says "let’s park that." It is now parked forever, which is what you wanted.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it.

title: MONDAY INBOX
text: 9AM. You open your laptop to 78 unread emails, three "URGENT" flags, and a calendar that is one solid block of colour until Thursday. The cursor blinks. It knows.

go.msg: You select all, archive, and decide anything important will come back. Bold. Reckless. Weirdly freeing. Two of those emails will indeed come back, louder.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it.

go.msg: You sort by sender, star the real ones, and clear the noise. It takes forty minutes and the satisfaction of a tidy inbox lasts nearly that long.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it.

title: THE COFFEE QUEUE
text: 8:55AM. The office coffee machine has a queue of six and a sign reading "BEAN HOPPER EMPTY — ask Reception (Reception is also empty)." Monday is testing you before you’ve even sat down.

go.msg: You find the beans, refill the hopper, and become an instant office legend. Six people love you. The machine rewards you with the first, best cup.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it.

choices.label: GIVE UP, DRINK THE BAD TEA

go.msg: You retreat to the sad tea bags nobody claims. It tastes of warm cardboard and lowered expectations. But you are, technically, caffeinated. Sort of.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it.

text.t: 9AM. "YOUR PASSWORD HAS EXPIRED." On a Monday. To you. The system does not care that you own a meaningful slice of the company. It wants twelve characters, one symbol, and your soul.
9AM. "YOUR PASSWORD HAS EXPIRED. Choose a new one." It must differ from your last 24 passwords, contain a symbol, and not resemble anything you could ever remember. Monday could not wait.

go.msg: You let the manager generate 20 random characters and save it. You will never know what your own password is, which is exactly the point.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it. (Starting strong: a password manager is the single best habit here.)

choices.label: ADD A "1" TO THE OLD ONE

go.msg: Autumn2024! becomes Autumn2024!1. Technically new. Spiritually identical. Every attacker’s first guess is your last password plus a number.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it. Predictable tweaks (+1, +!) are the first thing password-crackers try.

title: THE COMMUTE IN
text: 8:45AM. You arrive to find the office door propped open with a fire extinguisher and a friendly stranger holding two coffees: "Oh thank god — can you badge me in? Hands full! I’m new, start today." He does not have a badge. He has excellent coffee.

choices.label: BADGE HIM IN. HE SEEMS NICE.

go.msg: You tap him through. He thanks you warmly and disappears toward the server room, never to be seen at any desk, ever. Nice, it turns out, is a tactic.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it. That was tailgating — the coffee was the disguise. Everyone badges themselves in, no exceptions.

go.msg: You hold firm, politely. He sighs, the friendliness evaporates a little too fast, and he heads for reception — or rather, doesn’t. You start the week one social-engineer up.
go.tip: Welcome to the trail. Watch your three meters — and trust nothing with a link in it. Holding the badge line while staying polite is exactly the muscle this week trains.
